The SEO Growth OS checklist

The recurring SEO work I can help automate, the decisions it supports and the output you receive.

This is a guide, not an audit. Requesting it does not run anything on your website. Website changes are always reviewed and approved by you before anything goes live.

This checklist describes what SEO Growth OS is designed to cover. The capability names describe the work; they are not a claim that every workflow is already configured for your site. Available checks and automation are confirmed during setup.

What it can take off your weekly task list

  • Checking Search Console for pages gaining or losing visibility, and why.
  • Rechecking broken links, redirects and indexing after changes to your site.
  • Spotting pages that are seen in search but rarely clicked.
  • Drafting page briefs and internal link suggestions for your approval.
  • Checking whether selected AI answers mention or cite your business.
  • Keeping a dated record of what changed, and whether it is live.

How each capability runs

  • Scheduled check runs again on a schedule once the required tools, access and schedule are configured and tested.
  • Automated draft + human review the system prepares findings or drafts; a person reviews them before anything is used.
  • Manual review needs a person to judge, with the system organising the evidence.

Specific checks and automations

15 capabilities in six areas. Each shows what it checks, what can run automatically after setup, what you receive and what needs your review.

1. Website health

Is the website reachable, working and easy for search engines to read?

Crawl and indexing checks

Scheduled check

What it checks

Broken URLs, redirect chains, robots directives, noindex tags, canonical URLs and sitemap inclusion.

What can run automatically

Repeat the configured URL checks and compare the results with the previous run.

What you receive

The affected URLs, the issue found on each and a recommended next action.

What needs your review

Which fixes to make, and when.

Needs: Your public website; Search Console for Google’s view of indexing.

Page speed monitoring

Scheduled check

What it checks

Lab performance tests on key pages, plus real-visitor speed data where Google has enough of it.

What can run automatically

Retest the agreed pages and compare with earlier results.

What you receive

Pages that slowed down or improved, with the figures and the likely causes to look at.

What needs your review

Whether a fix is worth the development time.

Needs: Your public website; Google’s field data where available.

Structured data checks

Automated draft + human review

What it checks

Whether page markup is valid, free of errors and suited to the page.

What can run automatically

Validate markup on a schedule and draft new or corrected markup.

What you receive

The errors found and draft markup for the pages that need it.

What needs your review

That the details are accurate; your developer adds and tests the markup.

Needs: Your public website.

Key journeys and forms

Manual review

What it checks

Whether enquiry or booking journeys work on phones and desktops.

What can run automatically

Page availability can be rechecked; the journey itself is reviewed by a person.

What you receive

The steps that failed or caused confusion, with notes on each.

What needs your review

Test submissions happen only with your permission.

Needs: Your public website.

Related specialist capabilities: Technical SEO, Sitemaps and Discovery, Page Performance, Structured Data.

2. Search performance

Which pages and searches bring visibility and visits, and how is that changing?

Search performance monitoring

Scheduled check

What it checks

Page and query impressions, clicks, click-through rate and average position across comparable periods, with country filters.

What can run automatically

Collect connected search data, compare periods and flag changes for investigation.

What you receive

A shortlist of pages gaining or losing visibility, with the supporting figures.

What needs your review

Which changes are worth investigating.

Needs: Access to Google Search Console.

Local visibility tracking

Scheduled check

What it checks

Business Profile details and categories, and where you appear for searches in specific locations.

What can run automatically

Repeat location-specific observations where a suitable tracking tool is set up.

What you receive

Dated observations by location, plus gaps in your profile.

What needs your review

Profile changes before they are made.

Needs: Your Google Business Profile; a location tracking tool where required, which may have its own cost.

Competitor and opportunity research

Manual review

What it checks

Which competitor pages appear for your topics, and where the gaps are.

What can run automatically

Collect search data for the agreed topics.

What you receive

A short list of opportunities, with the evidence behind each.

What needs your review

Which opportunities fit your business.

Needs: Third-party search data, which may have its own cost.

Related specialist capabilities: Search Console Analysis, Local Search, Competitor Research.

3. Content

Do your pages explain what you offer and answer the questions customers ask?

Content opportunity review

Automated draft + human review

What it checks

Pages receiving impressions but few clicks, unanswered customer questions and possible overlap between pages.

What can run automatically

Identify candidates from the available data and prepare draft recommendations.

What you receive

A page-specific brief covering what to change and why.

What needs your review

The brief, and any wording, before it is used.

Needs: Your public website; Search Console for impressions and clicks.

Internal linking review

Automated draft + human review

What it checks

Links pointing to your priority pages, the wording of those links and relevant places to add new ones.

What can run automatically

Inspect crawlable links and prepare suggested additions.

What you receive

The source page, destination page and suggested link wording, for approval.

What needs your review

Each suggested link before it is added.

Needs: Your public website.

Page basics

Scheduled check

What it checks

Missing, duplicated or unclear titles, descriptions and headings on important pages.

What can run automatically

Recheck the agreed pages and flag new problems.

What you receive

A list of pages with the issue and a suggested fix.

What needs your review

The final wording.

Needs: Your public website.

Related specialist capabilities: Content Review, Internal Linking, On-page SEO.

4. AI visibility

Can AI tools understand your pages, and does your business appear for the questions that matter?

AI visibility tracking

Scheduled check

What it checks

Whether selected AI answers mention your business, cite your pages or describe your services accurately.

What can run automatically

Repeat supported checks and keep dated observations; other platforms need browser or manual review.

What you receive

For each check: the question, platform, date, observed answer and any citation.

What needs your review

Whether an answer is accurate, and what to do about it.

Needs: An agreed question list and access to the selected AI tools; some tools may have their own cost.

Answer readiness review

Manual review

What it checks

Whether key pages give clear, direct answers that AI tools can understand and cite.

What can run automatically

Draft suggestions can be prepared; the judgement is made by a person.

What you receive

Page-by-page notes and suggested edits.

What needs your review

Every edit before it is published.

Needs: Your public website and your knowledge of the business.

Related specialist capabilities: AI Search Visibility, Answer Readiness.

5. Measurement

Can the figures be trusted before anyone draws conclusions from them?

Lead measurement review

Automated draft + human review

What it checks

Whether recorded lead events correspond to real enquiries, whether test activity is included, and where evidence is missing.

What can run automatically

Collect the available figures and flag discrepancies for review.

What you receive

A clear explanation of which figures can support decisions and what needs checking.

What needs your review

Which actions count as a result, and any change to tracking.

Needs: Google Analytics and Tag Manager access; CRM or booking records with your permission.

Related specialist capabilities: Measurement Review.

6. Progress

What changed, what is still open, and what needs your approval?

Change verification

Scheduled check

What it checks

Whether an approved edit is live and meets its acceptance checks.

What can run automatically

Recheck observable page changes and update their status.

What you receive

A record showing each change as live, partly live, not yet live or unable to verify.

What needs your review

Anything that could not be verified.

Needs: Your public website and any connected data.

Change record and summaries

Automated draft + human review

What it checks

What was found, recommended, approved and changed, and what remains open.

What can run automatically

Keep a dated record and prepare a recurring summary.

What you receive

A short summary of what changed, what is unresolved and what needs your approval.

What needs your review

The summary before it is shared with anyone else.

Needs: Built from each run.

Related specialist capabilities: Change Monitoring, Reporting.

What a completed run gives you

Findings

Issues grouped as broken, missing or underperforming, with shared causes combined into one finding.

Priorities

Each recommendation weighed on severity, opportunity, strength of evidence, risk and effort, without one combined score.

Draft briefs and changes

Page briefs, link suggestions and draft markup, ready for your approval, each with a way to check it was done.

A change record

What was approved, what is live, and what could not be checked. Missing evidence is listed, never estimated.

A real example from HelpMeMarketing

From finding to a ready-to-use brief. A run on my own website, November 2026.

What the run found
SEO Growth OS identified a commercial page with limited search visibility, checked its indexing status and reviewed its internal links.
What it prepared
A brief identifying the pages to edit and the proposed link wording.
What happened next
The change required approval. Once approved, links were added from two related pages and went live on 10 November 2026. Implementation verification and search impact were tracked separately.

This shows the process on my own site. It is not a client result or proof of a ranking change.

What setup requires

  • Access to the data sources you want included, such as Search Console, Google Analytics, Tag Manager or your Business Profile.
  • An agreed list of checks, pages and, for AI visibility, the questions to track.
  • A schedule, and a test run to confirm each check works before it is relied on.
  • Any third-party tools the chosen checks need; some have their own cost.
  • Your approval before any website change goes live.

What it does not do

  • Promise rankings, traffic or AI citations.
  • Publish website changes without your approval.
  • Run without setup and the access each check needs.
  • Fill gaps with estimates when data is not available.
